The life of Harry S. Truman begins far from where the story usually starts. He was eligible for reelection in 1952 but he chose not to run due to poor polling. Subsequently, Truman went into a retirement marked by the founding of his presidential library and the publication of his memoirs.

Harry S. Truman was not born famous — the early years shaped everything that followed. The people who knew Harry S. Truman young describe someone already restless. The family lived in Lamar until Harry was ten months old, when they moved to a farm near Harrisonville, Missouri. They next moved to Belton and in 1887 to his grandparents' 600-acre (240 ha) farm in Grandview.

What Harry S. Truman built in the middle years is what the name still stands for.
